acceptance_criteria: Suppression checked pre-send. Webhook signatures verified. SES + one other provider tested with fixture payloads. Admin endpoint present.
description:
## Why this issue exists

When an email bounces (address does not exist, mailbox full, domain unreachable) or a recipient marks it as spam (complaint), the sending provider posts a webhook notification. Without processing these notifications stoa will:

1. Keep attempting delivery to addresses that will never accept mail, degrading sending reputation
2. Violate CAN-SPAM and GDPR requirements to honour unsubscribe/complaint signals promptly
3. Accumulate ISP complaints that eventually result in IP/domain blacklisting

This epic depends on the OutboundMailer abstraction (stoa-jom01 follow-on) because each provider has a different webhook format and authentication mechanism.

## What needs to be done

### Phase 1 — Suppression list

Add a `suppression` table to the stoa-mail schema:

```sql
CREATE TABLE suppression (
    email        TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('bounce_permanent', 'bounce_transient', 'complaint', 'manual')),
    provider     TEXT NOT NULL,
    occurred_at  BIGINT NOT NULL,
    raw_payload  JSONB,
    PRIMARY KEY (email, reason)
);
```

Before any outbound send, check the suppression list. If the recipient address has a `bounce_permanent` or `complaint` entry, skip delivery and log an `audit=true` event.

### Phase 2 — Webhook endpoint

Add a webhook handler to the stoa-mail axum router at `POST /webhooks/mail/{provider}`.

Implement webhook parsers for each HTTP API provider (behind the same feature flags as the provider impls):

- **SES**: SNS notification via HTTP POST. Verify SNS message signature before processing. Parse `Bounce` and `Complaint` notification types.
- **SendGrid**: Event Webhook. Verify `X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Signature` ECDSA signature.
- **Mailgun**: Webhook. Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature using webhook signing key.
- **Postmark**: Webhook. Verify via shared secret in `X-Postmark-Token` header (constant-time compare).

On verified bounce/complaint: upsert into suppression table; emit `audit=true` tracing event.

On signature verification failure: return 403, emit warning log, increment `webhook_sig_invalid_total{provider}` counter. Do not process payload.

### Phase 3 — Transient bounce retry policy

Transient bounces (mailbox full, greylisted, temporary server failure) should be retried with exponential backoff. Add retry metadata to the outbound queue:

- Max retries: configurable (default 5)
- Backoff: 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h, 24h
- After max retries: upsert as `bounce_transient` in suppression with a TTL (default 7 days)

### Phase 4 — Suppression list management API

Expose JMAP-style (or simple REST) admin endpoints:
- `GET /admin/suppression` — list suppressed addresses
- `DELETE /admin/suppression/{email}` — remove from suppression (e.g. after user confirms opt-in)
- Emit `audit=true` event on every suppression add/remove

## Acceptance criteria

- Suppression list checked before every outbound send
- Permanent bounce and complaint entries block future sends to that address
- Webhook endpoints verify provider signatures before processing payload
- SES and at least one other provider webhook parser implemented and tested with fixture payloads
- Transient bounce retried with backoff; eventually suppressed
- Admin endpoint allows removing a suppressed address

## Design notes

- Webhook payloads must be stored (raw_payload JSONB) for audit purposes — regulated customers need to demonstrate they acted on complaints within required timeframes (CAN-SPAM: 10 days; GDPR: without undue delay).
- Signature verification must use constant-time comparison (subtle::ConstantTimeEq) where applicable.
- The suppression table is per-instance, not per-user — a bounce on any account suppresses that address for all future sends from this stoa instance.
design: Suppression list is the right shared primitive. Webhook auth must be verified before any DB write — an unauthenticated webhook could be used to suppress arbitrary addresses (DoS on outbound delivery).
title: Outbound mail: bounce and complaint webhook processing
